texts.title: Hej! Jag heter Elin
texts.summaryFr: Elin, thirty-two, introduces herself: her town, Västerås, her little family, her job as a nurse and her hobbies.
texts.grammarFr: Present tense (är, har, heter, bor); personal pronouns (jag, du, han, hon, vi); short affirmative sentences and V2 word order (På lördagar simmar vi)

texts.title: En kaffe och en kanelbulle, tack
texts.titleFr: A coffee and a cinnamon bun, please
texts.summaryFr: At a café counter, Maja orders a coffee and chooses a cinnamon bun from the treats Ali offers her; she stays to have her fika there and pays by card.
texts.grammarFr: Simple questions (vad, vill du … ?); “jag vill ha”, “kan jag få”; politeness (tack, varsågod, tack så mycket)

texts.title: Var är Måns?
texts.summaryFr: One morning, little Leo looks everywhere for his cat Måns: under the bed, in the kitchen, behind the sofa, in the garden… He finally finds him, asleep in the basket of clean laundry.
texts.grammarFr: Prepositions of place (i, på, under, bakom); negation with inte (inte där, inte där heller); present tense; V2 inversion (I köket letar han…)

texts.title: Fyra årstider i Sverige
texts.summaryFr: A short informative text about the four Swedish seasons, month by month: the cold, dark winter, spring when the snow melts, the bright summer when the sun sets very late (and not at all in the North), and the colourful, rainy autumn.
texts.grammarFr: “det är” (det är kallt) / “det finns” (det finns mycket snö); seasons and months (lowercase); basic adjectives in the neuter and plural (kallt, mörkt, ljust; gröna, gula, röda)

texts.title: Min morgon
texts.summaryFr: Anton describes his morning hour by hour: waking up at half past six, the shower, a very Swedish breakfast (filmjölk, crispbread with cheese, coffee), then a twenty-minute bike ride to work.
texts.grammarFr: Telling the time (klockan sju, halv sju, halv åtta, tio i åtta); time adverbs (först, sedan, sist, då, nu) and V2 inversion (Först duschar jag)

texts.title: I mataffären
texts.summaryFr: At the supermarket, Fatima asks Hugo, an employee, where to find the milk, butter, bread, eggs and bananas. At the end, he lets her taste a new cheese.
texts.grammarFr: “Var finns … ?”; definite form (mjölken, brödet) and plural of common nouns (ostar, bananer, äpplen, ägg); quantities (två liter, ett paket, en bit)

texts.title: Snögubben
texts.summaryFr: Alva and Sam build a snowman with a carrot and a red scarf. The next morning, he is also wearing a blue hat and yellow glasses: Dad lent him his own.
texts.grammarFr: Adjective agreement (en stor mage, ett litet huvud, svarta stenar); colours; parts of the body (huvud, ögon, näsa, mage)

texts.title: Varför är husen röda?
texts.summaryFr: In the Swedish countryside, many wooden houses are red with white corners. Their paint, “Falu red”, is made from residues of an old copper mine; it is cheap, easy to apply and protects the wood.
texts.grammarFr: Agreement of colour adjectives (röd, rött, röda; vit, vitt, vita); “det finns” (there is/are); simple numbers (två, tusen)

texts.title: Min nya lägenhet
texts.summaryFr: Amir shows his new two-room flat in Malmö: the kitchen, the living room, the bedroom, the bathroom, the furniture and the view from the balcony over the sea and the bridge to Denmark.
texts.grammarFr: Definite singular form (köket, rummet, soffan, balkongen); prepositions of place (bredvid, mellan, framför, vid); agreement of the predicative adjective (köket är litet, vardagsrummet är stort)

texts.title: Ursäkta, hur kommer jag till stationen?
texts.titleFr: Excuse me, how do I get to the station?
texts.summaryFr: Erik has just arrived in town and asks Leila how to get to the station. She shows him the way to the stop, tells him to take bus number four and explains that you buy the ticket in an app, not from the driver.
texts.grammarFr: Imperative (gå, ta, sväng); directions (rakt fram, till vänster, till höger); numbers (fyra, tio); questions with hur, var, vilken

texts.title: Den nya grannen
texts.summaryFr: Wilma, seven, meets Mateo, a boy who has come from Chile and doesn't speak Swedish yet. Thanks to a football, they play together and each learns a word of the other's language.
texts.grammarFr: Negation (svarar inte, pratar inte … än); yes/no questions (Vill du spela? Kommer du i morgon?); verbs of movement in the present (springer, går, kommer)

texts.title: Djur i den svenska skogen
texts.summaryFr: A short informative text about the animals of the Swedish forest – the moose, the fox, the mountain hare, the squirrel, the bear, the wolf and the reindeer: what they eat and where they live.
texts.grammarFr: Indefinite plural of nouns (en älg – älgar, en björn – björnar, en ekorre – ekorrar; irregular: en mus – möss, en nöt – nötter; ett djur – djur); “det finns” (there is/are) and inversion; present

texts.title: Fredagsmys hemma hos oss
texts.summaryFr: Linnea, who lives in Västerås, explains the word fredagsmys and describes her family's Friday-night ritual: tacos, crisps and sweets, then a film on the sofa under a blanket.
texts.grammarFr: Days of the week; “brukar” + infinitive; “på fredagar”; subject-verb inversion (V2) after “På fredagar”, “Då”, “För mig”

texts.title: Ska vi ses på lördag?
texts.summaryFr: On the phone, Ebba suggests to Yusuf that they go to the swimming pool on Saturday. He isn't free in the morning, so they pick another time and a meeting place, and Yusuf's little sister will come too.
texts.grammarFr: Future with ska; days and times (klockan tio, kvart i två); suggestions and questions (“ska vi …?”, “kan du …?”, “får hon …?”)

texts.title: Ett paket till Ella
texts.summaryFr: Ella finds a small parcel outside the door with no sender's name. A book? A game? Inside there are red mittens and a letter from her grandmother, who lives in Umeå.
texts.grammarFr: Possessives (min, mitt, mina; din, dina); object pronouns (honom, henne, dem); present; subject-verb inversion (V2) after “Framför dörren”, “Där”, “Nu”

texts.title: Pannkakor på söndag
texts.summaryFr: A family makes pannkakor, Swedish pancakes, every Sunday: who does what, the ingredients, and how to eat them.
texts.grammarFr: Present; V2 word order after “på söndagar”; “ska” + infinitive; “behöver” + noun; “min” (possessive); plural adjectives (tunna, gula, goda)

texts.title: Vilket väder!
texts.summaryFr: Two neighbors meet on the stairs: it's raining again, and Olle advises Lina to take her umbrella.
texts.grammarFr: Present; “det regnar”; future with “blir”; imperative “ta med dig”; interjections (ja, jaså, precis, alltså)

texts.title: Färjan till Gotland
texts.summaryFr: A family goes on vacation to Gotland by ferry: the little brother runs on the deck, the father suggests eating, and the island appears after a few hours.
texts.grammarFr: Present; “åka” and “åker med”; “ska” + infinitive; “efter några timmar”; quotes with “säger”; V2 word order

texts.title: Midsommar i Sverige
texts.summaryFr: A simple introduction to Midsommar, the great Swedish summer festival: the maypole, dancing, flowers, and the meal of herring and strawberries.
texts.grammarFr: Present; -s passive (firas); indefinite pronoun “man” + verb; “på en fredag”; “det är ljust”; adjectives (ljus, glad, dekorerad)

texts.title: Min dag på bageriet
texts.summaryFr: Sanna, a baker in a small town, describes her day: she starts very early, makes bread and buns, and loves her job.
texts.grammarFr: Present; “klockan” + time; time adverbs (först, sedan, ibland); V2 word order; “mig” and “mina”; “från” + time

texts.title: Den blå jackan
texts.summaryFr: Dilan is looking for a jacket in a clothing store: it doesn't come in green, but the blue one fits her perfectly.
texts.grammarFr: Present; “Har ni … i grönt?” (color with “i”); “passar”; “Vilken storlek”; “där borta”; adjective forms (blå, blått)

texts.title: Lena springer i parken
texts.summaryFr: Lena wants to get stronger: she starts running in the park, a little at first, then farther and farther, and ends up proud of herself.
texts.grammarFr: Present; perfect “har sprungit”; “ger inte upp”; comparative (starkare, längre); “efter en månad”; V2 word order

texts.title: Lördagsgodis
texts.summaryFr: In Sweden, Saturday is candy day: a simple family ritual where children pick a little of everything themselves.
texts.grammarFr: Present; “en gång i veckan”; “lite av varje”; plural (barn, familjer); adverbs (oftast, fortfarande); “sitter i soffan”

texts.title: Vi är tre syskon
texts.summaryFr: Malin introduces her family: her big brother Johan, her little sister Saga, and her job as a dentist.
texts.grammarFr: Present; possessives (min, mina); “går i” + grade; “gillar” + noun; reciprocal “varandra”; “som” + profession without article

texts.title: Ett rum för två nätter
texts.summaryFr: At the reception of a hotel in Lund, Ingrid books a room with a balcony for two nights and receives her key card.
texts.grammarFr: Present; “Har du … ?”; ordinals (tredje); “på namnet”; “där borta”; polite expressions (välkommen, detsamma)

texts.title: Vi sorterar och pantar
texts.titleFr: We sort our waste and return deposit bottles
texts.summaryFr: The Berg family from Örebro explain how they sort their waste at home and return deposit cans and bottles to the supermarket, where their son Elias keeps the deposit money.
texts.grammarFr: Modal verbs (måste, ska, kan, får); “för att” + infinitive; inversion after a fronted object (Glaset måste vi…, Dem tar vi med…)

texts.title: Fel dag i tvättstugan
texts.titleFr: The Wrong Day in the Laundry Room
texts.summaryFr: Birgitta finds her neighbor Samir's laundry in the machine during her slot in the building's laundry room. The booking board shows that Samir got the day wrong; he apologizes and the two neighbors reach a friendly arrangement.
texts.grammarFr: Preterit (bokade, satte, läste); perfect (det har hänt); imperative (kom, behåll); apologies and polite phrases (förlåt, ingen fara, vad snällt)

texts.title: Trollet som inte kunde sova
texts.summaryFr: An old troll, Gorm, can no longer sleep since humans built a noisy road near his rock. A brave little girl, Stina, takes him at night to a quiet cave at the very top of the mountain.
texts.grammarFr: Preterit of strong verbs (sov, gick, såg, blev); subordinate clause with “när”; inversion after a fronted time expression (En kväll plockade…, Samma natt gick…)

texts.title: Allemansrätten – naturen är till för alla
texts.titleFr: The Right of Public Access – Nature Belongs to Everyone
texts.summaryFr: A simple text explaining allemansrätt, the right that lets everyone enjoy nature in Sweden: what you're allowed to do, what is forbidden, and the golden rule “don't disturb, don't destroy”.
texts.grammarFr: “får” (to be allowed to), “får inte” (not to be allowed to), “måste” (must) + infinitive; indefinite pronoun “man” (one, you); conditions with “om” (if); inversion after a fronted subordinate clause or object (Om man vill…, måste man…; dem får man inte…)

texts.title: Ingen har kontanter längre
texts.summaryFr: Lisa explains that she hardly uses cash anymore: she pays by card, pays her friends back with the Swish app and even pays that way at the school bake sale. Only her grandmother stays loyal to banknotes.
texts.grammarFr: Perfect (har använt, har slutat, har betalat); subordinate clause with “eftersom” and placement of “inte” (eftersom hon inte har…); comparative (snabbare, enklare, roligare än)

texts.title: På apoteket
texts.summaryFr: Alice has a cold and a sore throat. At the pharmacy, Mehmet asks her a few questions, recommends lozenges, rest and tea, and tells her to call the health centre if it doesn't get better.
texts.grammarFr: Modals for advice (du ska, du bör); questions with hur länge and hur ofta; polite imperative (läs, drick, ta det lugnt, är du snäll); perfect (har haft)

texts.title: Utelåst på balkongen
texts.summaryFr: One January morning, Bosse steps out onto his balcony in his pyjamas and the wind slams the door shut behind him. Nobody understands that he needs help, except Elias, the eight-year-old boy next door, who calls the caretaker.
texts.grammarFr: Preterit (vaknade, gick, stod) and pluperfect (hade snöat, hade slagit igen); temporal clauses (när, innan, efter att); ute/ut, inne/in (position or movement)

texts.title: Midsommar – sommarens största fest
texts.summaryFr: An informative text about Swedish Midsummer: its date, the decorated maypole and the ring dances, the flower crowns, the traditional meal, and an old belief about seven flowers under the pillow.
texts.grammarFr: Dates and ordinal numbers (den nittonde, den tjugofemte); the pronoun “man”; preterit for old traditions (förr trodde man, plockade, lade); superlatives (största, bästa, som längst)

texts.title: Min första vecka på SFI
texts.summaryFr: Camille, a French-speaking Belgian living in Gothenburg, describes her first week of Swedish for Immigrants (SFI) classes: a very international class, difficult pronunciation (å, ä, ö and the sj sound), and her first Swedish words in a shop.
texts.grammarFr: Preterit (flyttade, började, fick, använde, förstod) and perfect (har gått); clauses with “eftersom”, “att”, “när”; frequency adverbs (alltid, ofta, aldrig); inversion after “I augusti”, “I går”, “Men när …”

texts.title: Hur äter du din semla?
texts.titleFr: How do you eat your semla?
texts.summaryFr: On Shrove Tuesday (fettisdagen), Jonas brings semlor for the coffee break. With Petra, he explains to Amira, who has never tried one, how to eat them, and the two colleagues disagree about the best place in town.
texts.grammarFr: Comparative and superlative (godare, godast; bra, bättre, bäst/bästa); giving your opinion: jag tycker att …, jag tror att …; the pronoun “man”

texts.title: Nattåget norrut
texts.summaryFr: On the night train from Stockholm to Luleå, Moa shares her compartment with Elliot. They talk all night in front of the snowy forest, see the northern lights and, on arrival, exchange numbers.
texts.grammarFr: Preterit (steg, satte, log, skrev); subordinate clauses with “när”, “att” and “innan”; reflexive verbs (sätta sig, känna sig); “för att” + infinitive

texts.title: Lucia – ljus i decembermörkret
texts.titleFr: Lucia – Light in the December Night
texts.summaryFr: An informative text about Saint Lucy's Day, celebrated in Sweden on 13 December: the procession in white, the crown of candles, the songs, the saffron lussekatter, and the link between this celebration and light in the depths of winter.
texts.grammarFr: Ordinal numbers and dates (den trettonde december); definite plural form (ljusen, tärnorna, barnen, sångerna); perfect (har övat, har bakat) and preterit (var, trodde)

texts.title: Sportlov i fjällen
texts.summaryFr: Twelve-year-old Lukas describes the sportlov week (winter holiday) he spent with his family in a mountain cabin in Jämtland: downhill skiing, cross-country skiing, hot chocolate and a snowstorm.
texts.grammarFr: Perfect and preterit (har varit, har börjat / åkte, var); “för … sedan” (ago); adverbs and time expressions (först, efteråt, nästa morgon, redan, igen)

texts.title: Hattar, haklappar och kräftor
texts.summaryFr: Linnea, Mikael and Omar are planning a crayfish party in the garden. Omar has never been to one: they explain the bibs, the paper hats and the moon-shaped lanterns to him, then put him in charge of the cheese pie… and a song.
texts.grammarFr: Future (ska, kommer att); “behöver”; imperative and sharing out tasks

texts.title: Mysteriet med prinsesstårtan
texts.titleFr: The Mystery of the Princess Cake
texts.summaryFr: At the office, the princess cake bought for the boss's fiftieth birthday disappears from the fridge. Johanna investigates: every colleague has an alibi, but green crumbs lead her to the security guard's dog.
texts.grammarFr: Preterit; simple reported speech (hon sa att …); relative pronoun “som”

texts.title: Pappa är föräldraledig
texts.summaryFr: Fredrik describes the nearly six months of parental leave he has spent with his daughter Alva since his partner went back to work: the park, the parent-and-baby group at the library, and everything he has learned.
texts.grammarFr: Subordinate clauses with medan, som, fast, när, innan; perfect (har varit, har lärt mig) and pluperfect (hade varit, hade aldrig förstått); future with kommer att

texts.title: Jag tror att foten är stukad
texts.titleFr: I think I've sprained my ankle
texts.summaryFr: Rasmus twisted his ankle playing floorball. He calls the health centre, where the nurse Tove asks him questions, advises rest, ice and keeping his foot raised, and tells him when to call back.
texts.grammarFr: Indirect questions (om, hur, när); perfect; advice with “ska” and “borde”

texts.title: Tomten på Ekbacka gård
texts.summaryFr: A young family from Stockholm moves to an old farm in Småland. The neighbour advises them to leave porridge with butter out for the tomte on Christmas Eve; they forget, and strange things happen until they put their mistake right.
texts.grammarFr: Pluperfect (hade glömt); conditional “om”; narrative preterit

texts.title: Systembolaget – en butik med ett uppdrag
texts.titleFr: Systembolaget, a shop with a mission
texts.summaryFr: Informative article about Systembolaget, the state alcohol retail monopoly in Sweden: what it sells, its rules (minimum age twenty, closed on Sundays, no special offers), its public health mission and the arguments for and against.
texts.grammarFr: The -s passive (säljs, ägs, dricks, får säljas); relative clauses with “som”; vocabulary about society

texts.title: Valborg i Uppsala
texts.summaryFr: A student describes how he will celebrate his first Valborg in Uppsala on 30 April: a raft race on the Fyris river, white caps at three o'clock, a picnic in the park, a choir and a big bonfire in the evening.
texts.grammarFr: Future (kommer att); subordinate clauses with “innan”, “medan”; definite adjectives (den stora brasan)

texts.title: Berätta lite om dig själv
texts.titleFr: Tell us a bit about yourself
texts.summaryFr: Ibrahim, an electrician, has a job interview at a company in Norrköping with Karin, the manager, and Lars, a team leader: his background, his reasons for changing jobs, the working hours and the atmosphere in the team.
texts.grammarFr: Reported speech (sa att …, berättade att …); talking about your experience in the perfect (har jobbat, har dragit, har satt upp); sentence adverbs (faktiskt, egentligen)

texts.title: Robotdammsugaren som ville se världen
texts.titleFr: The robot vacuum that wanted to see the world
texts.summaryFr: Dammi, a robot vacuum that knows every crumb in its flat by heart, takes advantage of a door left open to explore the building. It meets a cat, rides the lift down to the basement… and its battery starts running low.
texts.grammarFr: Conditional (skulle vilja, skulle aldrig se); reported speech (frågade vad …, förklarade att …); particle verbs (sätta på, stänga av, följa med, ta slut)

texts.title: Vasaloppet – nio mil på skidor
texts.summaryFr: Every first Sunday in March, thousands of skiers cover 90 km from Sälen to Mora. The article tells of Gustav Vasa's flight in 1520, the origin of the race created in 1922, and describes today's race: classic style, blueberry soup at the refreshment stations and the motto on the finish arch.
texts.grammarFr: Numbers and dates (den första söndagen i mars; 1520 is read femtonhundratjugo, 1500-talet = the 16th century); superlative (största, mest kända, snabbaste); passive in -s (skickades, valdes, arrangerades, åks, serveras); historical preterit (kom, flydde, ångrade sig, hann ikapp)

texts.title: Studenten – den stora dagen
texts.summaryFr: Tilda tells about the day she finished upper secondary school: breakfast with the class, running out (utspring) in front of families holding up baby photos, a ride through town on a decorated truck, then her plans for the fall.
texts.grammarFr: Future plans (ska, tänker); temporal clauses; adjective + noun in the definite form

texts.title: Ska vi klä ut oss till påskkärringar?
texts.titleFr: Shall we dress up as Easter witches?
texts.summaryFr: Malin gets ready for Easter with her children Arvid and Siri: birch branches decorated with feathers, eggs to paint, dressing up as little Easter witches to trade drawings for candy at the neighbors' – and the old legend of the Blåkulla witches.
texts.grammarFr: Particle verbs (klä ut sig, hänga upp); “ska vi … ?”; clauses with “om”

texts.title: Skeppet som sjönk
texts.summaryFr: On 10 August 1628, fourteen-year-old Olof is a ship's boy aboard the Vasa, the king's new warship. A few minutes after setting off, the ship capsizes and sinks in the middle of Stockholm harbour. More than three centuries later, the wreck is raised and put on display in a museum.
texts.grammarFr: Narrative preterit (låg, sköt, sjönk, flöt); pluperfect (hade sett, hade fått, hade lärt sig, hade vuxit upp); subordinate clauses with “fast” and “medan”; s-passive (lyftes upp)

texts.title: Samerna – ett folk i fyra länder
texts.titleFr: The Sami – One People in Four Countries
texts.summaryFr: An article about the Sami, the Indigenous people of Sápmi, spread across Norway, Sweden, Finland and Russia: their languages, reindeer herding (which involves only a minority), duodji handicraft, joik, the Sami parliaments and the national day on 6 February.
texts.grammarFr: s-passive; relative clauses; “både … och”, “varken … eller”

texts.title: Sommar i stugan
texts.summaryFr: A young woman describes her family's summers in a little red cottage by a lake in Värmland: water from the well, an outhouse at the end of the garden, swimming, mosquitoes and card games on rainy days – and why so many Swedes love this simple life.
texts.grammarFr: “brukar” + infinitive and the habitual present; conditionals with “om” (real and hypothetical: om jag fick …, skulle vi …); memories in the preterit

texts.title: Loppis på lördag
texts.summaryFr: One Saturday, at a village flea market, Hanna falls in love with an old green armchair. With her more skeptical friend Felix, she haggles with Göran, an elderly seller, who ends up throwing in some porcelain cups – and even offers to deliver the armchair in exchange for a coffee.
texts.grammarFr: Comparatives (äldre än, dyrare än, fler än, bättre än, lika … som, ännu bättre); negotiating politely (skulle du kunna … ?); demonstratives (den här, den där, de här, de där)

texts.title: Det knackar i väggen
texts.summaryFr: The narrator and her friend Maja stay in an old country railway station that has become a hostel. At night, at twelve past three, there's knocking in the wall; the owner tells the story of a former stationmaster. The narrator finds a rational explanation… but two details make her doubt it.
texts.grammarFr: Pluperfect (hade varit, hade somnat, hade stannat); subordinate clauses with “medan” and “som om”; adverbs of manner (försiktigt, tyst, regelbundet, långsamt, förvånat)

texts.title: Att säga du till chefen
texts.titleFr: On First-Name Terms with the Boss
texts.summaryFr: Julien, a French engineer living in Linköping, tells with wry amusement what surprised him about Swedish work culture: being on first-name terms with the CEO, the flat hierarchy and consensus decisions, the sacred fika, offices emptying by four o'clock, and long parental leave.
texts.grammarFr: Nuanced connectors (däremot, dessutom, snarare, ändå, dock); passive with “bli” (blev tagen, blir ifrågasatta) and with -s (fattas, förankras, töms, ses); idiomatic work expressions (säga sitt, tycka till, tacka nej, i längden)

texts.title: Tåg eller flyg till Italien?
texts.summaryFr: Ida and Viktor are planning their vacation in Bologna. She wants to go by train for the climate's sake (“flygskam”, flight shame); he dreads the length of the journey and missed connections. After a friendly argument, they find a compromise.
texts.grammarFr: Conditional (skulle skämmas, skulle kunna, skulle gå åt); concessive clauses with “trots att” and “även om” (V2 after the subordinate clause); position of “inte” and adverbs in the subordinate clause (att flygplatser inte är, trots att jag i princip håller med); argumentation

texts.title: Väskan på sista bussen
texts.titleFr: The Suitcase on the Last Bus
texts.summaryFr: Marianne, who drives the last bus in Göteborg, notices that a man in a gray coat leaves the same black suitcase under his seat at the terminus every night. Gloves, an evasive look, a warm suitcase with something sloshing inside: she suspects some kind of smuggling and starts her own investigation… until an unexpected discovery.
texts.grammarFr: Past participles (kvarlämnad, inslagna) and present participles (bultande) used as adjectives; pluperfect (hade kört, hade försvunnit); crime-fiction style (short sentences, clues, suspense)

texts.title: Ett hotell som smälter varje vår
texts.titleFr: A Hotel That Melts Every Spring
texts.summaryFr: A report from Jukkasjärvi, north of the Arctic Circle: every winter, a hotel is built there from the ice of the Torne River. Blocks harvested in March, walls of “snis”, rooms carved by artists from all over the world, a night at around minus five degrees… then the thaw in spring.
texts.grammarFr: -s passive (byggs, sågas ut, lyfts upp, förvaras, öppnas, belönas, sparas) and passive with “bli” (blir utvalda); past participles used as adjectives (välvda, frusen, täckt, byggt); descriptive vocabulary for reporting

texts.title: Det finns inget dåligt väder
texts.titleFr: There's no such thing as bad weather
texts.summaryFr: A city dweller describes her relationship with outdoor life: secretly picking chanterelles, a rainy night in an open shelter, her daughter whose preschool spends its days outdoors in all weathers – and what this connection to nature, open to everyone, says about Sweden. In the background, her grandmother's saying about bad weather and bad clothes.
texts.grammarFr: Idiomatic expressions (upp till öronen, på sätt och vis, vem som helst); “trots att” (concession); present participles after komma (kom gående, kommer springande och sjungande); -s passive (ses som)

texts.title: Årsstämman i bostadsrättsföreningen
texts.summaryFr: At their housing association's annual meeting, the chair Kerstin leads a debate between Dragan, who refuses to pay for other people's cars, and Josefin, who supports charging stations; separate votes are held on the solar panels and the charging stations, and both proposals are adopted.
texts.grammarFr: Meeting phrases (ordet är fritt, jag yrkar på, med tanke på, jag finner att); -s passive (höjdes, betalas av, bärs ut, har antagits); däremot, dessutom

texts.title: Minnesbanken
texts.summaryFr: In the near future, people can sell their memories. Buried in debt, Jonatan sells the memory of his first love, Elsa. But strange gaps appear in his life, and when he wants to buy the memory back, it is too late: it has already been resold.
texts.grammarFr: Past conditional (skulle ha kunnat) and past unreal conditional (om du hade kommit); present and past participles (leende, skrattande, efterfrågade, sålts vidare); embedded subordinate clauses

texts.title: Lagom är inte alltid bäst
texts.titleFr: The happy medium isn't always best
texts.summaryFr: In this opinion piece, the author acknowledges the virtues of lagom – moderation, sharing, a sense of balance – but argues that this ideal also holds back ambition, creative boldness and the expression of emotions. He doesn't want to abolish it, only to take it down from its pedestal.
texts.grammarFr: Argumentative connectors (visserligen … men, å ena sidan … å andra sidan, dessutom, inte bara … utan också); -s passive and passive with bli (sägs, används, möts, hållas, har skapats, bli sedd); idioms (sticka ut hakan, ta för sig, ta i från tårna)

texts.title: Julbordet – en konst i flera omgångar
texts.titleFr: The julbord, an art in several courses
texts.summaryFr: A humorous guide, addressed to a new colleague from abroad, to surviving their first company Christmas buffet: the order of the rounds (herring, salmon and cold meats, hot dishes, rice à la Malta), schnapps and its song or julmust, and the rules not to break.
texts.grammarFr: -s passive (serveras, äts, skärs, har griljerats, som blandats) and passive with bli (har blivit bjuden); sequencing words (först, därefter, sedan, slutligen); imperative; compound nouns (julskinka, revbensspjäll, risgrynsgröt)

texts.title: Bina på taket
texts.summaryFr: On a local radio show, journalist Sanna interviews Anders, who keeps bees on a roof in Södermalm, Stockholm: life in the hive, city honey, the role of pollinators, stings and tips for beginners.
texts.grammarFr: Interview questions; passive with -s and with bli (odlas, skördas, ställs upp, bli stucken, det hörs); conditional inversion (har man ingen plats …); technical compound nouns (bikupa, arbetsbin, arbetsfördelning, stadshonung, biodling)

texts.title: Brev från Minnesota
texts.summaryFr: In the 1880s, Karl, a young emigrant from Småland, writes three letters to his mother: the grueling crossing to New York, then clearing the land he obtained in Minnesota, and finally, as Christmas approaches, his homesickness and big news: he has married, is expecting a child and has decided to stay in America.
texts.grammarFr: Letter-writing style (Kära mor!, Din tillgivne son); pluperfect (hade lagt ner, hade tjänat, hade lovat, hade sparat ihop); past participles used as adjectives (rökta, fastgjutna, nybakade); old-fashioned expressions (for, Gud bevare dig, tjäna piga, tillgivne); inversion expressing a condition (Blir det en flicka, …)

texts.title: Nobelpriset – från dynamit till fredspris
texts.titleFr: The Nobel Prize – from dynamite to the Peace Prize
texts.summaryFr: A portrait of Alfred Nobel, chemist and inventor of dynamite, and the story of his 1895 will, which created the Nobel Prizes: first prizes in 1901, a ceremony in Stockholm every 10 December, the anniversary of his death, a banquet at the City Hall, and the Peace Prize awarded in Oslo.
texts.grammarFr: Passive in -s (riktas, patenterades, delas ut, pekades ut, kunde verkställas, serveras, utses) and with “bli” (blev kritiserat); past participles (återberättad, instiftat, förenade); dates (den 10 december, år 1900, året därpå)

texts.title: Ett år norr om polcirkeln
texts.titleFr: A Year North of the Arctic Circle
texts.summaryFr: A young doctor from Malmö describes her first year at the hospital in Gällivare: the midnight sun that keeps her awake, the polar night that is never completely dark, her first northern lights, the huge distances and locals who are reserved at first, until the day a colleague tells her: “Now you're one of us.”
texts.grammarFr: Concessives (trots att, även om); present and past participles used as adjectives (omtumlande, dansande, tejpade, kokt); “ju … desto” + comparative; unreal condition (som om det vore)

texts.title: Om strömmen går
texts.summaryFr: After a four-hour power cut in the middle of winter, Nora and Elias wonder what they should have at home to manage on their own for several days, as the authorities recommend: she methodically draws up the list (water, food that needs no cooking, a battery radio, blankets), while he thinks it's all over the top… before asking for chocolate.
texts.grammarFr: Hypotheticals (tänk om det hade varit, om … skulle hända, ifall … skulle); past conditional (Vad hade vi gjort då?); nuanced modals (borde, lär + perfect infinitive); passive after a modal (kan ätas)

texts.title: Sista dansen på logen
texts.titleFr: The Last Dance in the Barn
texts.summaryFr: One summer evening, at a barn dance, Gunnel, a seventy-year-old widow, meets Sture again, who had apparently stood her up on a date fifty years earlier. They discover that they had simply each been waiting by a different bridge – and they dance the last dance together.
texts.grammarFr: Free indirect speech (Vad gjorde hon här egentligen? Löjligt.); pluperfect in retrospective narration (hade stämt träff, hade väntat); participles (inklämd, nystrukna, konserverade); idiomatic expressions of feelings (hjärtat slog en volt, inte bry sig ett dugg, unna någon något)

texts.title: Året runt i skärgården
texts.summaryFr: A year-round resident of an island in the Stockholm archipelago describes her year: summer overrun by boaters, the quiet autumn, the winter when the ice cuts the island off from the mainland, the tiny school threatened with closure – and why this chosen isolation is not loneliness.
texts.grammarFr: Complex syntax (parenthetical clauses, conditional inversion: Blir någon sjuk får man…); -s passive (fylls, stängs, dras upp); figurative language (livlina, statister, två sidor av samma mynt); maritime and island vocabulary (gästhamn, brygga, udde, menföre); register variation

texts.title: Säger ni verkligen så?
texts.summaryFr: At a dinner in Stockholm, Mikaela, a Finland-Swede from Helsinki, Pontus, from Skåne, and Selma, from Stockholm, tease each other about the way they speak: the “semla” that is just a bread roll in Finland, Skåne words, the melody (or lack of it) and the r, then the place of Swedish in Finland and on Åland.
texts.grammarFr: Modal particles (ju, väl, nog); dialect variation (Finland-Swedish words: semla, fastlagsbulle, kiva; Skåne words: påg, tös, rälig); informal register (nja, liksom, alltså); particle verbs and reflexive verbs (hälsa på, anpassa sig, klara sig, skratta ihjäl sig)

texts.title: Mötet som aldrig tog slut
texts.summaryFr: In a government office, replacing cracked coffee cups turns into a saga: a working group, a survey, consultations and the search for consensus (“förankring”) drag on for seven weeks, under the increasingly ironic, then almost admiring, eye of an Italian consultant.
texts.grammarFr: Impersonal -s passive (beslutades, fördes fram, levererades); bureaucratic nominalizations (beslutsunderlag, svarsfrekvens, förankring); past conditional (skulle ha valt); irony and zeugma; verbal phrases (ta ställning, ställa sig bakom, fatta beslut)

texts.title: Jantelagen – en seglivad myt?
texts.titleFr: The Law of Jante – a persistent myth?
texts.summaryFr: An essay on the Law of Jante: born in 1933 in a novel by Aksel Sandemose as a satire of a stifling small town, it is used today to explain Scandinavian modesty, or even to brush aside any criticism. The author acknowledges its element of truth but shows what is mythical about it.
texts.grammarFr: Formal argumentation and connectors (förvisso, icke desto mindre, dessutom, därmed, på så vis, snarare) ; s-passive (åberopas, myntades, styrs, kritiseras) ; nominalizations (anspråkslöshet, förskjutning, försiktighet) ; relative vars ; att-clause as subject (Att begreppet … används … är …)

texts.title: Gotland utanför säsongen
texts.summaryFr: An account of a stay on Gotland in November: an empty ferry, Visby and its medieval wall deserted, far from the August crowds of Medieval Week, the wind-battered raukar of Fårö, the sheep and the medieval churches. The narrator discovers an island “without make-up”.
texts.grammarFr: Rich descriptive syntax (inversion after a fronted element: Där … satt nu ; Vid stranden reste sig …) ; past participles used as adjectives (igenbommade, staplade, förstenade, vitkalkad) ; s-passive (lösts upp, fylls, används) ; similes and metaphors (som en stad som just har vaknat, likt en samling förstenade jättar) ; particle verbs (ta emot, klä ut sig, dyka upp)

texts.title: Lönesamtalet
texts.summaryFr: At the annual salary review, Niklas puts forward his results and asks his boss Jenny for a raise that brings him closer to the market rate. Jenny points out the framework of the collective agreement and the pay criteria; after a silence, they agree on a compromise: an above-average raise now and a new meeting in the autumn, tied to new responsibilities.
texts.grammarFr: Professional register and negotiation phrases in the conditional (skulle jag vilja, vad skulle du säga om, vore det rimligt, borde) ; specialized vocabulary (lönesamtal, kollektivavtal, lönekriterier, löneökningar, lönestatistik) ; s-passive (skars ned, fördelas, syns) ; idiomatic expressions (gå obemärkt förbi, sticka under stol med, komma ikapp)

texts.title: Den sista vintern
texts.summaryFr: In a future where it no longer snows in southern Sweden, a grandfather tells his granddaughter Vera about the winters of his childhood; she doesn't believe him, until he shows her his old skates.
texts.grammarFr: Future in the past (skulle komma); past conditional (om han hade vetat, skulle han ha stannat); pluperfect; figurative language (similes, personification)

texts.title: Offentlighetsprincipen – frihet eller övervakning?
texts.titleFr: The principle of public access: freedom or surveillance?
texts.summaryFr: An opinion piece on the principle of public access to official documents, written into Swedish law as early as 1766: a bulwark against corruption, it also lets anyone find out their neighbour's income or address. The author acknowledges these abuses but defends the principle and targets the data trade instead.
texts.topicFr: Debate – the principle of public access
texts.grammarFr: Dense argumentation (förvisso, ändå, icke desto mindre, alltså); concession and refutation; legal terms (allmän handling, sekretess, insyn); conditional vore

texts.title: Bostadskön
texts.summaryFr: A man in his thirties ironically recounts his housing journey in Stockholm: signing up for the housing queue at eighteen, precarious sublets, shared flats, a first lease in a distant suburb, and the dilemma of whether to keep renting or buy a bostadsrätt apartment.
texts.grammarFr: Specialized housing vocabulary (förstahandskontrakt, andrahandskontrakt, hyresrätt, bostadsrätt, budgivning); irony; participial phrases (skrivet på baksidan…, uthyrd av…); -s passive

texts.title: Vargen – hot eller tillgång?
texts.summaryFr: In a radio debate hosted by Lena, Per, a sheep farmer from Värmland who has lost animals, calls for more hunting, while Aisha, a biologist, defends wolf protection and fencing; the discussion also reveals the divide between city and countryside.
texts.grammarFr: Debate with opposing views; polite interruptions and rephrasing (får jag bara säga, ursäkta men, fast); ecology vocabulary (rovdjur, licensjakt, inavel, revir); -s passive and passive with bli

texts.title: Det stora oväsendet
texts.summaryFr: Mora, 1669. Now an old woman, she remembers the summer she was nine: the children of the parish accused women of taking them to the witches' sabbath at Blåkulla, and an evasive answer she gave the pastor still weighs on her conscience.
texts.grammarFr: Slightly archaic language (ty, ej, sade, somliga, angivit); reported speech (att-clauses, om-clauses); pluperfect and omission of hade in subordinate clauses (att hon varit där, sedan de blivit ansatta)

texts.title: Vackrare vardagsvara – idén bakom svensk design
texts.titleFr: More Beautiful Everyday Things: the idea behind Swedish design
texts.summaryFr: An article tracing the roots of Swedish design: Ellen Key's ideal of “beauty for all”, the 1919 pamphlet Vackrare vardagsvara, the functionalism of the 1930 Stockholm Exhibition and flat-pack furniture; it then asks whether this “democratic” design is still a reality or mostly a brand image.
texts.grammarFr: Nominalisations (demokratiseringen, granskning, formgivning); vocabulary of aesthetics; historical argumentation; -s passive (förknippas, betraktades, marknadsförs); idiomatic expressions (rikta udden mot, falla i god jord)

texts.title: Ny medborgare den sjätte juni
texts.summaryFr: Nasrin came from Iran at the age of seven but only applied for Swedish citizenship twenty years later. She describes the ceremony held by her municipality on National Day and reflects on what “becoming Swedish” means in a country that celebrates its homeland with surprising restraint.
texts.grammarFr: Personal reflection; fixed subjunctive (Leve Sverige!, det vore); concessive clauses (även om, trots att, hur … än); inversion after a fronted subordinate clause; particle verbs (skicka in, brista ut, bli av med)

texts.title: Är Pippi en förebild?
texts.summaryFr: In their book club, Agnes, Isak and Milena reread Pippi Longstocking as adults: a free, anti-authoritarian heroine, or a little girl left to fend for herself? The debate shifts to the art of Astrid Lindgren, who speaks to children and adults alike.
texts.grammarFr: Literary analysis; nuances of opinion (å ena sidan … å andra sidan, snarare, fast, vare sig … eller); modal particles (ju, väl, nog, ändå, faktiskt); conditional clause without om (kallar vi …, gör vi …); passive after låta sig (låter sig styras)

texts.title: Dödsstädning
texts.summaryFr: At eighty-four, Ingrid takes on her "dödsstädning": sorting through her belongings to spare her children. A never-forgotten love letter, the coffee set for special occasions and a red ball gown each awaken a part of her life. But the object she finally decides to keep is not the one you would expect.
texts.topicFr: Literary short story – the great clear-out
texts.grammarFr: Literary narration in the past tense; free indirect speech and interior monologue; verbless sentences and ellipses (Ingen brådska. Så tunn.); pluperfect (hade sagt, hade varit menat); particle verbs (riva sönder, slå in, stå kvar, ställa tillbaka)

texts.title: Avståndets etik
texts.summaryFr: An ironic column on the Swedish art of keeping one's distance: the widely spaced queue at the bus stop, the bag placed on the next seat on the train, the queue ticket that spares you any negotiation, and the stairwell where you listen for the neighbour's footsteps so as not to run into them – ending with a self-deprecating punchline.
texts.grammarFr: Irony and self-deprecation; long sentences (fronted subordinate clause followed by inversion: Först när … lyfter vi); rare vocabulary (vågstycke, storsinthet, beseglat) and a coinage (revirdemokrati); particle verbs and reflexive verbs (slå sig ner, tränga sig före, slå igen, våga sig ut)

texts.title: Får man säga så?
texts.titleFr: Are you allowed to say that?
texts.summaryFr: At a dinner party, Gustav, an ironic purist, laments anglicisms and the pronoun “hen”; the linguist Vera and the young communications professional Theo reply with humour that the language has always borrowed and digested new words – and catch him red-handed using slang.
texts.grammarFr: Irony, allusions and innuendo; formal register (nåväl, förtjänar, parlerade) vs informal (asgod, pitcha, deal); idioms (ut med språket, utan att blinka, tappa sömnen över)

texts.title: Femtioårsdagen
texts.summaryFr: At his brother Mats's fiftieth birthday party, the narrator silently composes the vengeful speech he will never give: an unfair inheritance, a “stolen” wife… But the details he lets slip gradually reveal a very different story.
texts.grammarFr: Unreliable narrator and dramatic irony; conditional with skulle (skulle jag börja); free indirect speech; embedded subordinate clauses and cleft sentences (det är först när … som)

texts.title: Sagoskogen och kalhygget
texts.titleFr: The Fairy-Tale Forest and the Clear-Cut
texts.summaryFr: Essay on the Swedish forest: between the dream forest of the fairy tales illustrated by John Bauer and the industrial forest of plantations and clear-cuts, supporters and critics of forestry invoke the same forest. The real question: which one do Swedes love, and are they willing to pay for it?
texts.grammarFr: Dense argumentative prose (concession, contrast: fast, utan, alltså); -s passive (fälls, planteras, målades); cultural references; forestry vocabulary (kalhygge, gallring, virkesförråd, massaved)

texts.title: Juli, när Sverige stänger
texts.summaryFr: An ironic column about July, when all of Sweden goes on holiday: the legacy of industrial holidays, cascading out-of-office messages, lines of cars heading to summer houses – and Luca, an Italian living in Gothenburg, who discovers that no decision will be made before mid-August.
texts.grammarFr: Ironic column; hyperbole and comparisons; -s passive (tömdes, utnyttjas, drabbas); idioms (sitta i ryggmärgen, ladda batterierna, dra ner rullgardinen)

texts.title: Repetitionen
texts.summaryFr: At the theatre, the director Klara rehearses a break-up scene with Olle, a seasoned actor, and Saga, a young actress. Disagreements over interpretation slide into an old wound between Klara and Olle, until the scene finally finds its truth.
texts.grammarFr: Meta-theatre; shifting registers (stage jargon, colloquial language, condescending tone); nuanced imperatives and commands (var snälla, gör mig en tjänst och…, låt bli att, du får gärna, strunta i)

texts.title: Översättarens anmärkningar
texts.summaryFr: A Swedish translator annotates her translation of a French novel: her notes, technical at first (a title with a double meaning, formal address, an untranslatable word), gradually let her own life show through – her years in Lyon, her mother, a lost marriage – up to one final infidelity to the text.
texts.grammarFr: Metafiction; digressions; play on registers (låta sig + infinitive, past participles without auxiliary, relative clause with vilket)

texts.title: Myndighetsprosa och rätten att förstå
texts.titleFr: Bureaucratic prose and the right to understand
texts.summaryFr: A polemic against the jargon of Swedish public authorities: nominalizations, agentless passives and incomprehensible letters, illustrated by a pastiche of an official letter, even though the 2009 Language Act has long required language that is careful, simple and comprehensible. For the author, plain language is a question of democracy.
texts.grammarFr: Polemic; pastiche of bureaucratic language; nominalizations; -s passive without agent; set phrases (med anledning av, kan komma att)

texts.title: Surströmmingspremiären
texts.summaryFr: A columnist describes his first taste of surströmming, on the third Thursday of August, on the High Coast: bulging cans opened in a bucket of water, an apocalyptic smell, then the ritual of tunnbröd, potatoes, red onion and ice-cold milk – and the discovery of shared courage more than of a dish.
texts.grammarFr: Rare sensory vocabulary; humor and hyperbole; cultural references; -s passive (rullas ihop); comparisons (som om, som en …)

texts.title: Recensionen
texts.summaryFr: In the culture section of a daily newspaper, editor Ulrika, veteran critic Tomas and young journalist Nadia discuss a scathing review Tomas has written of the debut novel by a close friend of a colleague he has fallen out with. Amid understatements and digs, they weigh critical freedom against the appearance of a conflict of interest, until they reach a compromise.
texts.grammarFr: Journalistic jargon (gå in, partsinlägg, jäv); understatements and euphemisms (inte direkt, inte oangenäm, en smula); implicit argumentation; unreal conditional (om jag hade skrivit … hade någon frågat)

texts.title: Lärjungens dagbok
texts.summaryFr: The fictional diary of a young ship's chaplain, a disciple of Carl Linnaeus, who sails to Canton on an East India Company ship: botanical wonder, a flying fish sacrificed to the sailors' appetite, fever and bloodletting, doubts about the master's glory – and a small blue flower secretly named after his sister.
texts.topicFr: Historical vignette – a disciple of Linnaeus
texts.grammarFr: Pastiche of 18th-century language (plural verb forms gingo, voro, åto; ej, icke, ty, blott, hvarje; masculine -e ending: bäste); botanical vocabulary; diary style

texts.title: Den svenska kärleksteorin
texts.summaryFr: An essay on the thesis of historians Henrik Berggren and Lars Trägårdh: in Sweden, the state and the individual have formed an alliance that frees everyone from family dependence, in the name of a love that can only be true between autonomous equals. Freedom or loneliness? The author explores the paradoxes of the folkhem.
texts.grammarFr: Conceptual essay: abstract nouns (beroende, oberoende, tacksamhetsskuld, godtycke); compound participles (skandalomsusad, mellanliggande, fastkedjad); inversion after a fronted adverbial (Därav…, Kanske ligger…); concessive and contrastive constructions (snarare än, varken … eller, inte … utan)

texts.title: Kolonilottens lagar
texts.titleFr: The laws of the allotment garden
texts.summaryFr: As the new owner of a cabin in an allotment garden, the narrator discovers fussy rules, the spring inspection and a neighbor who criticizes through compliments, before tasting the joy of gooseberries. He sees in it the legacy of an educational project born at the end of the 19th century.
texts.grammarFr: Ironic column: pastiche of regulations (få ej, ska hållas, med … avses, slår fast att); -s passive; botanical vocabulary (krusbär, svartvinbär, maskros, rädisa); irony through antiphrasis and euphemism (inte utan ömhet)

texts.title: Kvällen före disputationen
texts.summaryFr: On the eve of her public defense, Elsa, a PhD student in history, rehearses in her kitchen with her supervisor Gunnar and her friend Amina the questions the opponent might ask. Between academic advice, teasing about the “spikning” and anxiety, the question of her future remains open.
texts.grammarFr: Academic register (ironic formal address with ni/er, källkritik, ramverk) and intimate register; innuendo and ellipsis; idioms (gå åt skogen, tänka på stående fot, hålla fast vid, ta det på måndag); future with kommer att

texts.title: Flyttfåglarna
texts.summaryFr: One October morning, a man returns to Ottenby, at the southern tip of the island of Öland, to watch the bird migration as he did as a child with his father, who died in the spring. Amid cranes, birds of prey and memories of silences, his father's notebooks bring him a belated reconciliation.
texts.grammarFr: Poetic prose in the narrative present, with flashbacks in the preterit and pluperfect; past conditional (skulle ha sagt, hade gillat); ellipses and verbless sentences (Rätt vind och fel år; Arter, antal, vindriktning); -s passive (återkallats); ornithological vocabulary (trana, ormvråk, sparvhök, rovfågel)
